discoveredAssets: localhost:8080 - IDOR Eats (Apache 2.4.41 PHP) - Port 8080 - Main food delivery web application
http://localhost:8080/ - Homepage (index.php) - Public entry point with restaurant showcase
http://localhost:8080/login.php - Public login page - Accepts POST via AJAX to /api/login.php
http://localhost:8080/register.php - Public registration page - Accepts POST via AJAX to /api/register.php
http://localhost:8080/profile.php - Protected profile page - Requires authentication, redirects to login
http://localhost:8080/api/ - Directory listing enabled - Exposes all API endpoints
http://localhost:8080/api/login.php - Authentication API endpoint - POST method required
http://localhost:8080/api/register.php - User registration API endpoint - POST method required
http://localhost:8080/api/search_restaurants.php - Public restaurant search API - GET with query parameter
http://localhost:8080/api/get_favorite_restaurants.php - Protected API - Returns user favorites, requires auth
http://localhost:8080/api/change_password.php - Protected API - Password change, requires auth
http://localhost:8080/static/ - Directory listing enabled - Contains images (restaurants, profiles)
http://localhost:8080/static/images/ - Image directory - 11 image files including restaurant images and profile.jpg

targets.objective: Test authentication bypass vulnerabilities including SQL injection, NoSQL injection, default credentials, and authentication logic flaws
targets.rationale: Critical authentication endpoint. POST endpoint accepting username and password. Should test for injection vulnerabilities, brute force protection, and proper session management

targets.objective: Test registration security including input validation, password strength enforcement, account enumeration, and authorization checks
targets.rationale: Public registration endpoint without apparent input validation. Should verify password requirements, email validation, and duplicate account prevention

targets.objective: Test for injection vulnerabilities (SQL, NoSQL, command injection), authorization flaws, and information disclosure in query parameter handling
targets.rationale: Public API endpoint accepting 'query' parameter. Should test for SQL injection, NoSQL injection, and potential IDOR if restaurant IDs are exposed in responses

targets.objective: Test for IDOR vulnerabilities, horizontal privilege escalation, and unauthorized data access between users
targets.rationale: Protected endpoint returning user-specific data. Highly likely to contain IDOR vulnerabilities if user identification relies on predictable parameters

targets.objective: Test for IDOR vulnerabilities, unauthorized access to other users' profiles, and sensitive data exposure in profile pages
targets.rationale: Protected profile page for authenticated users. Should test for IDOR via user ID manipulation if accessible through URL parameters or other means

targets.objective: Test for CSRF protection, old password verification, weak password requirements, and horizontal privilege escalation in password changes
targets.rationale: Password change endpoint requiring authentication. Should verify CSRF tokens, proper authorization checks, and whether users can change other users' passwords

targets.objective: Test login form for CSRF vulnerabilities, account enumeration, rate limiting, and client-side security issues
targets.rationale: Public login page. Should test for CSRF tokens, brute force protection, and information disclosure through error messages

targets.objective: Test registration form for CSRF vulnerabilities, input validation bypass, and business logic flaws
targets.rationale: Public registration page. Should verify CSRF protection, input validation, and potential for account takeover attacks

targets.objective: Enumerate all available API endpoints and test for unintended endpoint access, HTTP method manipulation, and information disclosure
targets.rationale: Directory listing enabled on /api/ directory exposes all endpoint names. Should identify any additional endpoints and test each for vulnerabilities

targets.objective: Test homepage for XSS, CSRF, client-side vulnerabilities, and business logic flaws in search functionality
targets.rationale: Main entry point. Should verify security of search functionality and any user input handling

keyFindings: [CRITICAL] Directory listing enabled on /api/ - All API endpoints are publicly discoverable (change_password.php, get_favorite_restaurants.php, login.php, register.php, search_restaurants.php)
[CRITICAL] Directory listing enabled on /static/ and /static/images/ - Exposes application structure and available resources
[HIGH] Application named 'IDOR Eats' - Suggests deliberate IDOR vulnerabilities for testing/training purposes
[HIGH] Public API endpoint /api/search_restaurants.php - Returns restaurant data including IDs without authentication required
[HIGH] Protected endpoints using PHP sessions - /api/get_favorite_restaurants.php and /api/change_password.php require authentication
[HIGH] Multiple authentication endpoints - /api/login.php and /api/register.php are public and accept POST requests
[MEDIUM] No apparent CSRF protection on forms - login and register forms use AJAX without visible CSRF tokens
[MEDIUM] Profile page redirects unauthenticated users to login - Indicates authorization controls but should test for bypasses
[MEDIUM] API endpoints return JSON responses - Structured data format facilitates automated testing
[MEDIUM] No HTTPS/TLS used - Application runs over plain HTTP on localhost
